title: Fletcher Henderson's many keys again
summary: Crawford repeats that Henderson wrote in all keys and it took Roy Eldridge a long time to adjust.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you -- did you think that Fletcher Henderson's use of a lot of different keys had an effect on what kind of writing Sy Oliver did for Fletcher's band?
Yeah. I remember you were telling me earlier that you remember the time when most of the tunes were written, and most of the tunes the guys played were in keys of B flat and C.
Yeah, around in there, but Fletcher Henderson, he put them in all kind of sharps and flats. That

is why Roy Eldridge -- took him a long time to get used to that band, because he played in regular keys, B flat, E flat, C's, F's, and like that. When you go into those A flats and A sharps, all that kind of stuff, took him a long time to get with it. He admitted it, too. He said they're playing in too many keys. Yeah. Great band, Fletcher's band. Saw a lot of young drummers in here.
